concepts.name: Sources of business law
concepts.summary: Recall that business obligations come from statutes, regulations, court decisions and contracts, and that rules vary by jurisdiction.

concepts.name: Types of business structure
concepts.summary: Name the main structures (sole proprietorship, partnership, limited liability company, corporation) and describe how they differ in broad terms.

concepts.name: Legal personality
concepts.summary: Explain that some entities are legally separate from their owners and can own property, sign contracts and be sued in their own name.

concepts.name: Contract elements
concepts.summary: Explain that a contract needs offer, acceptance, consideration, intent to be bound and capacity, and recognise each in a simple example.

concepts.name: Business liability
concepts.summary: Understand that a business can be held responsible for harm, debts or breaches, and that owners may or may not be personally exposed.

concepts.name: Types of intellectual property
concepts.summary: Recall the main IP forms (trademarks, copyright, patents, trade secrets) and the kind of thing each protects.

concepts.name: Employee versus contractor
concepts.summary: Understand that people working for a business are classed as employees or independent contractors, with different legal rights and obligations.

concepts.name: Licences, permits and registration
concepts.summary: Recall that businesses often must register, hold licences and file returns to operate lawfully.

misconceptions.text: A verbal agreement is never a legally binding contract.
Registering a company name automatically gives full trademark protection.
Any business structure fully protects the owner's personal assets.

concepts.name: Offer, acceptance and written terms
concepts.summary: Apply formation rules to emails, quotes and signed documents to decide whether and when a binding agreement exists.

concepts.name: Common contract clauses
concepts.summary: Read and apply clauses on payment, termination, warranties, confidentiality and governing law to a given agreement.

concepts.name: Breach and remedies
concepts.summary: Identify a breach and match it to likely remedies such as damages, termination or specific performance.

concepts.name: Limited liability protection
concepts.summary: Explain how limited liability structures shield owners from business debts and why personal guarantees limit that shield.

concepts.name: Choosing a structure
concepts.summary: Apply criteria such as liability, tax treatment, cost and funding needs to pick a suitable structure for a small business scenario.

concepts.name: Trademark and copyright ownership
concepts.summary: Determine who owns a logo, brand name or creative work, including work made by employees or freelancers.

concepts.name: Employment basics
concepts.summary: Apply core employer duties such as written terms, minimum pay, working time, non-discrimination and workplace safety to simple cases.

concepts.name: Data privacy obligations
concepts.summary: Understand that collecting customer or staff data brings duties on notice, consent, security and retention.

misconceptions.text: If a contract is signed, every clause in it is automatically enforceable.
Whoever pays for a logo or website design automatically owns the copyright.
Forming an LLC or corporation means the owner can never be personally liable.

concepts.name: Contract risk allocation
concepts.summary: Analyse how indemnities, limitation of liability and warranty clauses shift risk between parties and spot one-sided terms.

concepts.name: Contract defects and defences
concepts.summary: Analyse whether misrepresentation, mistake, duress or illegality undermines an agreement.

concepts.name: Piercing the corporate veil
concepts.summary: Analyse facts such as commingled funds, undercapitalisation and fraud that lead courts to hold owners personally liable.

concepts.name: Directors' and partners' duties
concepts.summary: Apply duties of care, loyalty and good faith to decisions by directors, officers or partners.

concepts.name: Vicarious and product liability
concepts.summary: Analyse when a business is liable for employee conduct, negligence or defective products.

concepts.name: IP protection and infringement
concepts.summary: Analyse whether a use infringes IP and which registration, licensing or confidentiality steps best protect an asset.

concepts.name: Worker classification and termination
concepts.summary: Analyse classification tests and dismissal, redundancy and restrictive covenant risks in employment relationships.

concepts.name: Compliance programme design
concepts.summary: Apply a risk-based approach to map applicable regulations (tax, consumer, data, sector rules) to policies, records and deadlines.

misconceptions.text: A limitation of liability clause always protects a party regardless of how it behaved.
Calling someone a contractor in the agreement settles their legal status.
Separate legal personality means a court will never look behind the company to its owners.

concepts.name: Negotiation strategy for contracts
concepts.summary: Evaluate which terms matter most in a deal given leverage, risk and commercial goals, and decide where to concede or insist.

concepts.name: Dispute resolution options
concepts.summary: Evaluate negotiation, mediation, arbitration and litigation by cost, speed, confidentiality and enforceability.

concepts.name: Structuring for growth and exit
concepts.summary: Evaluate how structure, shareholder agreements, vesting and investor terms affect control, liability and exit.

concepts.name: IP strategy and licensing
concepts.summary: Evaluate licensing, assignment and registration choices across jurisdictions to balance protection, revenue and cost.

concepts.name: Cross-border legal issues
concepts.summary: Analyse how choice of law, jurisdiction, export rules and local employment or tax rules affect cross-border operations.

concepts.name: Legal risk assessment
concepts.summary: Evaluate the likelihood and impact of legal risks and judge which to avoid, insure, mitigate or accept.

concepts.name: Instructing and managing lawyers
aliases: knowing when to seek legal advice
concepts.summary: Judge when a matter needs a lawyer, what kind, and how to brief and control scope and cost.

misconceptions.text: Arbitration is always cheaper and faster than court.
Using a template contract removes the need to check it against the specific deal and jurisdiction.
Legal advice is only needed once a dispute has already started.

concepts.name: Bespoke contract architecture
concepts.summary: Design contract frameworks that align incentives, allocate uncertainty and stay workable over a long relationship.

concepts.name: Enterprise legal risk framework
concepts.summary: Create a governance framework linking board oversight, policies, controls and escalation to the organisation's legal risks.

concepts.name: Evaluating regulatory change
concepts.summary: Evaluate how new or conflicting regulation affects the business model and decide when to adapt, lobby or restructure.

concepts.name: Transaction and restructuring design
concepts.summary: Design acquisitions, financings or reorganisations that manage liability, diligence findings, tax and stakeholder interests.

concepts.name: Crisis and insolvency decisions
concepts.summary: Evaluate legal duties and options during financial distress, investigations or major incidents, including directors' exposure.

concepts.name: Global IP and data strategy
concepts.summary: Create integrated strategies for IP ownership, data transfers and enforcement that hold across several legal systems.

concepts.name: Legal ethics and culture
concepts.summary: Evaluate how incentives, whistleblowing channels and tone from leadership shape real compliance beyond the letter of the law.

misconceptions.text: Full compliance with the written rules is enough to eliminate legal and reputational risk.
A more detailed contract always reduces risk more than a simpler one.
Directors are protected from personal exposure once a company is in distress, because the entity bears the losses.
